title: DNS: names to addresses
summary: Query a DNS server by hand with dig, read different record types, then point a PC at it.

nodes.ns: the office DNS server for dojo.lab, 10.14.1.53

tasks.title: Ask a server directly
tasks.text: From **pc**, ask the DNS server `10.14.1.53` for the address (A record) of `intranet.dojo.lab`. What IP comes back?
hints: `dig @SERVER NAME` sends one query to one server and prints the full answer.
`dig @10.14.1.53 intranet.dojo.lab`, or add `+short` for just the answer.

tasks.title: Aliases
tasks.text: `www.dojo.lab` is not a real host, it is a **CNAME** (an alias). Which name does it point to?
hints: `dig @10.14.1.53 www.dojo.lab` and look in the ANSWER SECTION for the CNAME line.

tasks.title: Where does mail go?
tasks.text: Mail for a domain is delivered to the host in its **MX** record. Which host receives mail for `dojo.lab`?
hints: Put the record type after the name: `dig @10.14.1.53 dojo.lab MX`.

tasks.title: Records that hold text
tasks.text: **TXT** records hold free text (used for email security, domain verification, and sometimes leaked secrets). Read the TXT record of `_flag.dojo.lab`.

tasks.title: Use it as the resolver
tasks.text: Typing `@10.14.1.53` every time is not how PCs work. Configure **pc** so ordinary programs resolve `dojo.lab` names through `10.14.1.53`: `getent hosts vault.dojo.lab` must return `10.14.1.99`.

checks.fail_msg: getent hosts vault.dojo.lab does not return 10.14.1.99 yet.

hints: Linux reads its DNS servers from `/etc/resolv.conf`. Look at it first: `cat /etc/resolv.conf`.
Replace the `nameserver` line with `nameserver 10.14.1.53`. For example: `echo 'nameserver 10.14.1.53' > /etc/resolv.conf`.
